[Pedagogy review · Suggestion · variation-sequence · pf-842e2a9fee]
At p3-guided: Append parts under the existing derivative-and-interpretation instruction. Add only this instruction: 'Predict whether the volume is increasing or decreasing and whether that change is speeding up or slowing down before calculating.' At t=10 use, in order: (c) V=2000+40t+t²; (d) V=2000+40t−t²; (e) V=2000−40t−t²; (f) V=2000−40t+t². Answers (V′, V″): (c) (60,2), increasing and speeding up; (d) (20,−2), increasing and slowing down; (e) (−60,−2), decreasing and speeding up; (f) (−20,2), decreasing and slowing down, with units L/min and L/min². Keep coefficient magnitudes, initial volume and evaluation time fixed; change one sign between neighbours. Follow with (g) V=2000−3t²+t³/10 at t=5. Answer: V′=−22.5 L/min, V″=−3 L/min²; decreasing and speeding up.

After p19-guided-part-b add parts: (i) 'Find the particle's displacement between t=1 and t=4.' Answer: −9 m. (ii) 'How far does the particle travel while its velocity is negative during this interval?' Answer: 16 m. (iii) 'Explain why its distance travelled exceeds its displacement by 32 m.'
